questions.question: How do == and === differ, and which is usually clearer for comparisons?
keyPoints: === checks type as well as value
Choose intentionally when coercion is needed
questions.modelAnswer: The loose equality operator may convert operands before comparing them, while strict equality does not. Strict equality is usually clearer because the compared types remain explicit and implicit coercion is avoided.

questions.question: Why does the order of conditions matter in an if / else if chain?
keyPoints: Only the first true branch runs
Broad earlier conditions can shadow narrow later ones
Order tests from most specific or highest threshold as appropriate
Use mutually exclusive branches when practical
questions.modelAnswer: An if / else if chain checks conditions in order and runs only the first matching branch. If a broad condition comes first, it can prevent a later, more specific condition from ever being reached.

questions.question: When is a ternary expression appropriate, and when should a regular if statement be preferred?
keyPoints: Ternary selects one of two expressions
It can be concise for a simple value choice
Use if for multiple statements or complex branches
questions.modelAnswer: A ternary works well when a simple condition selects between two values in an expression. For multiple actions or complicated decisions, an if statement is easier to read and maintain.
